signals.text: In addition, it is important that the curriculum includes rich opportunities for children to develop their spatial reasoning skills across all areas of mathematics including shape, space and measures.

We aim to develop a broad range of skills in using and applying mathematics, by building on the ability to show initiative in solving problems in a wide range of contexts, including the new or unusual.

 Pupils use sentence stems to respectfully challenge ideas such as “I disagree with ___ because…” Nurture and Citizenship  Maths is linked to real-life where appropriate, to develop future life skills and give the learning context.

Maths Calculation Policy Amended: Summer 2025 This calculation policy sets out the methods used to help our pupils with calculations and has been devised to meet requirements of the National Curriculum 2014 for the teaching and learning of mathematics.

By providing frequent and varied opportunities to build and apply this understanding – such as using manipulatives, including small pebbles and tens frames for organising counting – children will develop a secure base of knowledge and vocabulary from which mastery of mathematics is built.

SEN Information For Parents
You will find attached some useful leaflets for parents.
If you would like to contact a member of the SEN Team, please email us on inclusionteam@hovejun.brighton-hove.sch.uk where your email will be forwarded to a member of our team who will reply to you.
Please click here for information on the Local Offer.
The local offer is the provision available across education, health and social care for children and young people with SEND, and their families, in a local area. Information on the local offer must be set out in one place. This is outlined in the SEND code of practice, 2014. The local offer has 2 key purposes:

HLF-SEND-Information-Report-September-2025

Smartphone Free Childhood Campaign
Welcome to the Smartphone Free Childhood (SFC) info hub for West Hove Infants and Hove Juniors.
This webpage is run by a small group of parents, and aimed at rallying support for those who would like to:
* Think about delaying the introduction of smartphones for their children: Sign our pact here. * Explore alternative options. * Find support within our school and local community, and connect with other like minded parents and carers.
Watch this short video to find out more about why we are doing this.
This page is focused only on school-relevant information. For up-to-date research, local events, and info on the Brighton & Hove, and Sussex-wide movements, please visit the Sussex SFC website here.
Our SFC Parent Support WhatsApp Groups:
Use the QR codes below or click on these links to join our school-wide WhatsApp groups:
* Portland Road site: https://chat.whatsapp.com/EHAccChfegl6OUUCkC7MMM
* Holland Road site: https://chat.whatsapp.com/CmBDzMPJH0X4MTRtmH3wde
Strength is in numbers and we are always looking for more people to join our working group!
Please get in touch via your school’s whatsapp group (links above) if you would like to find out more.
Our School Smartphone Survey:
In June 2024 we carried out a school-wide survey, showing overwhelming support for a pact to delay the introduction of smartphones, and feelings of concern from parents and carers about the impact of smartphones. Read our findings here, in the West Hove parent smartphone survey report.
Sign the Smartphone Free Childhood Parent Pact:
In response to the nation-wide outpouring of concern and support for a delay in the introduction of smartphones, the SFC movement has produced school-specific pacts.
Sign your name here, and signal your intention to delay giving your child a smartphone until they reach the age of 14. It’s voluntary and non-binding, but the more sign ups we get, the easier it will be to start changing the norm in our school, for our kids.
Sign the pact here, and see where we are on the Sussex leaderboards!
Useful Information, Links and Resources:
*Smartphone letter to families January 2025
* Parenting in the Digital Age, a brilliant information video for parents on how to navigate technology, especially smartphones by GP Dr Susie Davis
* BBC breakfast interview with headteacher, Tony Plunkett, and co-founder of Smartphone Free Childhood, Joe Ryrie, talking about the SFC Parent Pact, 26th September 2024
*National Summit on Education talk by Jonathon Haidt, containing the latest research into why social media and smartphones are causing an epidemic of mental illness amongst our young people
*‘The Anxious Generation’ book by Jonathon Haidt

Arbor for Parents
Arbor Parent Portal is a free-to-download app that keeps you connected to all of your child’s school news, either via instant messages sent straight to your smartphone or by email. It is easy, safe and convenient to use.
The Arbor App lets parents book parent/guardian consultation slots, track your child’s attendance, update your contact details and give parental consents e.g. photo permissions/walk home alone permissions/trip etc.
For further information, please see the letter below or click on this link.

Hove Partnership
Hove Cluster Core Curriculum Offer and Agreement
We would like to propose a ‘Core Curriculum Offer’, which we are happy to coordinate and organise within the cluster and review as a cluster on an annual basis.
Curriculum Offer and Agreement:
Release subject leaders for core curriculum meetings each term in English and maths. (Supply to be funded by the cluster)
Foundation curriculum meetings will be developed on a rolling programme, according to need and capacity. E.g. Geography would be a group that West Blatchington would like to set up and run, as this is linked to their SIP.
Each school to offer shadowing/mentoring of a subject leader from another school, as appropriate and identified through the cluster. (See survey feedback and next steps).
Curriculum cluster links identify specific CPD/training or initiatives either in house/external linked to the cluster’s development priorities
Support curriculum and training through offering one to two places for staff training/inset should it align with your areas of SIP each term.
